items.followUp: Explain the working of a switch in a computer network.

rubric.why: Checks the router’s basic function and the networks it connects.
rubric.description: Defines a router as a device that forwards data between networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it forwards data between different networks.

rubric.why: Checks how a router decides where to send data.
rubric.description: Explains that it uses addressing or routing information to choose a route.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct explanation of route selection.

rubric.why: Checks a common use of a router.
rubric.description: States that a router connects a local network to the internet or another network.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct connection or use.

rubric.why: Checks a further relevant feature of routers.
rubric.description: Mentions that routers can provide wired or wireless network connectivity.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct connectivity feature.

modelAnswer: A router is a networking device that forwards data packets between different networks.
It examines the destination IP address and uses routing information to select a suitable path for the data.
A router commonly connects a local area network (LAN) to the internet and allows devices on the network to communicate.
Routers may provide wired connections, wireless connections, or both.

items.followUp: Name and briefly explain any four types of software piracy.

rubric.why: Checks identification and explanation of softlifting.
rubric.description: Explains softlifting as installing or copying software beyond the terms of its licence.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming softlifting and describing unauthorised copying or installation.

rubric.why: Checks identification and explanation of client-server overuse.
rubric.description: Explains using more copies or users of network software than the licence permits.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this type and describing use beyond the licence limit.

rubric.why: Checks identification and explanation of hard-disk loading.
rubric.description: Explains that a seller installs unauthorised software on a computer before selling it.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this type and describing unauthorised preinstallation.

rubric.why: Checks identification and explanation of counterfeiting.
rubric.description: Explains making and selling unauthorised copies that imitate genuine software.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming this type and describing fake or unauthorised copies.

modelAnswer: Softlifting: making or installing extra copies of software in violation of its licence.
Client-server overuse: allowing more users to access network software than the licence permits.
Hard-disk loading: a computer seller installs unauthorised software on a computer before selling it.
Software counterfeiting: making and selling unauthorised copies that imitate genuine software.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm? State one feature of a good algorithm.

rubric.why: Checks that the student identifies a flowchart as a visual representation of a process or algorithm.
rubric.description: Defines a flowchart as a graphical representation of an algorithm or process.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the graphical-representation definition.

rubric.why: Checks for the symbols and flow that make up a flowchart.
rubric.description: Mentions standard symbols connected by arrows to show the sequence of steps.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the symbols and/or arrows showing step order.

modelAnswer: A flowchart is a graphical representation of an algorithm or process.
It uses standard symbols connected by arrows to show the sequence of steps.

items.followUp: How does an algorithm help a programmer develop a solution?

rubric.why: Checks that an algorithm provides an ordered set of instructions for solving a problem.
rubric.description: States that an algorithm gives step-by-step instructions to solve a problem.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the step-by-step solution idea.

rubric.why: Checks a practical benefit of planning a solution as an algorithm.
rubric.description: Explains that it helps organise the logic before coding and can make errors easier to find.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a relevant benefit such as planning logic or finding errors.

modelAnswer: An algorithm gives a clear, step-by-step sequence of instructions for solving a problem.
It helps organise the solution’s logic before programming and makes the steps easier to check for errors.

items.followUp: State two advantages of using a flowchart to represent an algorithm.

rubric.why: Checks that the student explains how a flowchart makes the solution easier to understand.
rubric.description: States that a flowchart presents the steps visually and clearly.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the clarity or visual-presentation benefit.

rubric.why: Checks for another practical benefit in problem solving.
rubric.description: States that a flowchart helps check or debug the solution, or communicate it to others.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for one valid additional benefit.

modelAnswer: A flowchart shows the steps of a solution visually, making the logic easier to understand.
It helps trace and check the steps for errors and makes the solution easier to communicate.

items.followUp: Draw a flowchart to calculate the perimeter of a rectangle.

rubric.why: Checks that the flowchart accepts the required measurements.
rubric.description: Shows input of the parallelogram’s base and perpendicular height.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the input step with both required values.

rubric.why: Checks the correct calculation and completion of the flowchart.
rubric.description: Calculates area as base multiplied by perpendicular height, displays the result, and ends.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the correct formula and an output/end step.

modelAnswer: Draw an oval labelled START.
Draw an input parallelogram labelled Input base b and perpendicular height h.
Draw a process rectangle labelled A = b × h.
Draw an output parallelogram labelled Display A.
Draw an oval labelled STOP.
Connect the symbols in order with arrows: START → Input → A = b × h → Display A → STOP.

items.followUp: What is HTML, and what does it use to mark up a web page?

rubric.why: Checks that markup is described as using tags to mark up content.
rubric.description: States that a markup language uses tags to mark or annotate content.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying tags and their marking-up function.

rubric.why: Checks the purpose of markup in a document or web page.
rubric.description: Explains that markup describes or controls the structure or presentation of a document or web page.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct purpose of markup.

modelAnswer: A markup language uses tags to mark or annotate parts of a document.
The tags describe the structure or presentation of content, such as a web page.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the href attribute in an HTML anchor tag?

rubric.why: Checks identification of the HTML anchor element.
rubric.description: Identifies the anchor as the HTML <a> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for correctly naming the anchor tag.

rubric.why: Checks the function of an anchor.
rubric.description: States that an anchor creates a hyperlink to another page or resource, usually using the href attribute.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for the hyperlink function.

modelAnswer: An anchor is an HTML element written with the <a> tag.
It creates a hyperlink to another web page or resource, with the destination specified by the href attribute.
